title: Windows B: rustc 1.99.1 crashes with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION during cargo check (second occurrence); find the likely cause without system changes
outcome: The most likely cause of Windows B's repeated rustc access-violation crashes is named with read-only evidence (hardware or memory, a damaged toolchain file, security software, or resource exhaustion), and any reinstall, restart or configuration change it needs is presented to Greg as a concrete proposal, so Windows B can return to the gate pool or stay out for a stated reason.
acceptance: The evidence from Windows B is collected read-only and preserved under .evidence on that host. It covers the Application and System event logs for the crash times (Application Error and WER entries for rustc.exe, WHEA-Logger, disk and memory-diagnostic events), Windows Defender operational events, the WER report archive entries, and the state of both crash targets (test-3104849c and the earlier 1098a838-a).

The toolchain on Windows B is compared with Central's identical rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3): rustc -vV, plus sha256 of rustc.exe and rustc_driver-58995fd3f1c8ecc6.dll (Central: BA03E3BA…AA72 and 49372CE0…D495, 206004736 bytes); a mismatch or a match is recorded.

The item names the most likely cause, or says it remains unknown, with the evidence that supports it. Any reinstall, restart, memory test or configuration change is a written proposal for Greg; none is performed.
